current_evidence: Atlas already contains self-reported sleep duration/insomnia and 2019 accelerometer sleep duration/efficiency; 2026 device GWAS adds night duration, efficiency, REM and NREM.
public_data_and_prior_art: 2026 Portas et al. reports 80,013 UKB Europeans; device-derived stage labels have moderate PSG concordance (kappa=0.32); existing multi-cohort PRS work compared questionnaire definitions across four external cohorts.
remaining_gap: No cohort-disjoint genetic comparison across clinical insomnia, self-report, and device sleep; formal between-phenotype contrasts require joint covariance, not separate rg estimates.
decision: High-value resource extension only if framed as construct/source comparison; do not claim new biology from adding the four overlapping UKB traits.
status: PARTIAL: existing evidence; no new fit

current_evidence: Frozen discovery extension already contains 1,200 global correlations across 100 outcomes and separate 1,200-test BH family; domain summaries are present.
public_data_and_prior_art: Portas et al. tested four device traits against ten health traits, including cardiometabolic, aging, memory, Alzheimer and Parkinson outcomes.
remaining_gap: No source-matched, harmonized disease-system contrast for new device traits; much of the selected outcome panel and biological interpretation overlaps published Portas analyses.
decision: Do not run a 400-test add-on as a broad scan. Reconsider only after a finite independent question and a frozen family are approved.
status: EXISTING breadth; broad extension not currently justified

current_evidence: Current Atlas primary result sources are overwhelmingly European; existing analyses do not establish transferability.
public_data_and_prior_art: Published multi-ancestry sleep-duration GWAS include UKB/MVP strata; six EUR, AFR and cross-population short/long files are publicly downloadable from Yale; the 2025 UKB+MVP quantitative study totals 646,218 but is predominantly European (98.4% UKB EUR; 84.9% MVP EUR).
remaining_gap: The Yale sleep files are not yet downloaded or schema/hash-verified, and no ancestry-matched disease-outcome panel, ancestry-specific LD-reference contract, or outcome overlap ledger has been established for an Atlas transferability analysis.
decision: Do not infer transferability from meta-analysis or significance counts. The Yale files make a future bounded sleep-source audit feasible; an Atlas disease-transferability analysis still needs ancestry-specific disease GWAS and compatible LD.
status: GAP: public sleep sources located; Atlas portability untested

current_evidence: 2026 device GWAS is age-adjusted and reports sex-specific results; its Catalog releases are combined-sex summaries.
public_data_and_prior_art: Portas et al. reports cross-sex rg of 0.98, 1.00, 0.97 and 0.84 (sleep efficiency, REM, night duration, NREM); four sex-heterogeneous loci. Authors label stratified locus results exploratory and request replication.
remaining_gap: No age-stratified summary-statistic set; sex-specific full genome-wide statistics not verified in the Catalog release reviewed here; age-adjusted is not age-stratified.
decision: Carry published estimates as prior evidence only. Do not re-run without the actual sex-stratified files and a calibrated cross-sex contrast.
status: PARTIAL: sex prior art; age comparison unsupported

current_evidence: Global LDSC correlation results exist in the frozen core and extension. Local architecture queue and readiness artifacts exist but do not admit a defensible local analysis under the current method/input contracts.
public_data_and_prior_art: Portas et al. reports global sleep-trait and sleep–health correlations and locus-level follow-up; this is not a local-rg analysis of the atlas's disease panel.
remaining_gap: No selected, independently justified locus/region plus method-matched LD, overlap, and regional variance inputs; broad scans would multiply tests without a precise question.
decision: Keep local analysis out of the current critical path. Admit only a targeted region question with an input and calibration contract.
status: GAP: global complete; local not scientifically admitted

current_evidence: Existing project mechanism, fine-mapping, and colocalization readiness ledgers do not admit new molecular claims from current atlas estimates.
public_data_and_prior_art: Portas et al. reports published locus prioritization, eQTL/colocalization and tissue analyses; no cell types passed Bonferroni correction.
remaining_gap: No new atlas-specific signal with source direction, independent replication, credible set and suitable molecular-QTL evidence all authenticated.
decision: Do not repeat broad enrichment or colocalization scans. Treat Portas mechanisms as prior art, not atlas discoveries.
status: GAP: published mechanism evidence; no new atlas mechanism

current_evidence: Existing 217-candidate review found 23 outcome-side positives sharing the discovery sleep source; these are not independent two-trait replications. QC and uncertainty holds remain explicit.
public_data_and_prior_art: The 2026 Portas GWAS is from UKB and overlaps the cohort underlying key Atlas sleep sources; it cannot supply cohort-independent sleep replication for them.
remaining_gap: No newly identified cohort-disjoint sleep source with compatible phenotype, ancestry, effective N, genome build, and auditable overlap was admitted.
decision: Retain qualified outcome-side validation labels. Do not promote results to independent replication or claim reliability gains.
status: ESSENTIAL GAP: no independent sleep-cohort replication

current_evidence: V7 compared four dated, row-level snapshots over 1,637 records: 361 qualified match-absent in those snapshots; no exact source/estimand class-A matches. V8 adds an interpretation-safeguard use case.
public_data_and_prior_art: Portas is a primary GWAS paper rather than a general-purpose association resource; it contains its own sleep–health analyses and is therefore prior art, not a like-for-like resource snapshot.
remaining_gap: No measured head-to-head researcher-utility advantage, resource-wide coverage claim, or license-cleared unified release.
decision: Keep the fixed-snapshot benchmark bounded. Do not enlarge denominators with a paper that is not a compatible resource export; retain usability and release claims as unresolved.
status: PARTIAL: bounded comparator audit complete; utility/release gap remains
